Streets, schools and getting around Hemlock Valley

items.t: The place: Hemlock Valley is the residential village at Sasquatch Mountain Resort (formerly the Hemlock ski area).

Governance: Hemlock Valley is unincorporated land in FVRD Electoral Area C; the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019) governs the plan area, and the FVRD administers that plan. The plan area is based on the Controlled Recreation Area (CRA) established by the Province of British Columbia in 2016 as part of approval of the Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan; the CRA carries the licence of occupation that lets the resort developer use Crown land for the purposes in the Resort Master Plan. Neighbourhood planning areas inside the OCP area are Hemlock West (the historic resort community), Hemlock East and Hemlock North, each to be detailed through neighbourhood plans as the resort expands.
Mailing reality vs governance: live-page listings in this sub-area carry both "Mission, BC V0M 1A1" and "Agassiz, BC V0M 1A1" mailing addresses — neither mailing town is the governing authority.

Neighbours and distances, per the OCP: the largest nearby town is Agassiz in the District of Kent, approximately 38 km from Hemlock Valley; Mission is approximately 55 km west; the Village of Harrison Hot Springs sits at the southern end of Harrison Lake, south of the plan area.
Per-sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level — there is no Hemlock median price in the permitted source.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: there is almost none to concentrate.

Transit: no public transit service to Hemlock Valley was confirmed on an official source: UNVERIFIED. Access is by road from the Agassiz / Harrison Mills side; the FVRD evacuation guide's evacuation route runs past Sts'ailes First Nation, Harrison Mills and sites along that route. The road's name, condition standard and winter maintenance responsibility on an official page: UNVERIFIED in the research pass.

Resort, as the OCP records it: the alpine ski hill (now Sasquatch Mountain Resort) consists of 4 ski lifts servicing 146.8 hectares of developed ski terrain on 35 named trails, on the south and southwest slopes, using a 100% natural snowpack; its Comfortable Carrying Capacity is approximately 1,150 skiers/boarders per day and its Balanced Resort Capacity 1,640 guests per day. Resort-operator claims rest only on the operator's own marketing and are UNVERIFIED here.

Community organisation: the Hemlock Valley Homeowners Association, established in 1980, is a non-profit that works on behalf of valley homeowners — a community association, not a strata corporation or a co-op tenure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Hemlock Valley

items.t: Form B diligence (the 1 strata complex above, and any strata unit in the valley): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Local plan — FVRD, not a city: the governing plan is the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019) for Electoral Area C, built on the provincially approved Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan and its 2016 Controlled Recreation Area. Servicing is a resort-community system administered in the FVRD plan framework, not City of Mission services; the OCP's Infrastructure & Services chapter covers water supply, sanitary sewer systems, utilities and communications, stormwater, snow clearing and storage, solid waste and emergency/protective services. Parcel-level servicing (which system a given lot is on, and its fees): UNVERIFIED.

Hazards and Development Permit Areas: the OCP carries a Hazard & Risk Management chapter including a Wildfire Interface Hazard section, and Development Permit Areas in Schedule I that include protection of development from hazardous conditions. Parcel-level hazard/DPA status: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the FVRD before valuing a slope lot.

RURAL property tax regime — explicitly different from Mission's and Chilliwack's: Hemlock Valley is unincorporated, so the owner receives the property tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays property taxes to the Province, not to the FVRD or any city. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, rural property taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Hemlock Valley

items.t: The mailing address lies twice (2026-11-01).

The tax penalty is the rural one, and it is staged. 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31 under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11 — a buyer cross-shopping a Mission city townhouse (flat 10% on July 3) and a Hemlock unit is comparing two different penalty regimes, two different payees, and two different plans.

The whole village exists because of a Crown licence. The Controlled Recreation Area was established by the Province in 2016 as part of approval of the Resort Master Plan, and it carries the licence of occupation that lets the resort developer use Crown land for the Master Plan's purposes — the resort's existence is a provincial tenure instrument, which is why the FVRD plan, not a municipal one, governs the village.

The expansion numbers are a vision, not a build-out schedule. The OCP records a phased vision toward 19,969 bed units and a Balanced Resort Capacity of 16,641 visitors per day, against a built base of 226 resort residential units (1,072 bed units) and a current Balanced Resort Capacity of 1,640 guests per day. The gap between those two pairs of numbers is the single most mis-sold fact in the valley.

Three Edelweiss Drive addresses are three different tenure stories. 20649 Edelweiss Drive reads as a townhouse in form with no tenure stated in its listing; 20668 Edelweiss Drive is expressly "NO STRATA" freehold fourplex product; and the directory's Rocky Bluff entries at 20619/20629 Edelweiss Drive are freehold strata with their built form UNCONFIRMED. A search that blurs the street blurs the diligence.

The homeowners have been organised since before the current resort name. The Hemlock Valley Homeowners Association was established in 1980 — the same year the building directory gives for the Enzian Way building — and works on behalf of valley homeowners as a non-profit.

There is an evacuation guide for this village. The FVRD publishes a Hemlock Valley Evacuation Guide whose route runs past Sts'ailes First Nation and Harrison Mills — a single-road mountain community plans its exit in writing, and a full-time buyer should read that document before the strata documents.

The ski hill runs on natural snow only. The OCP records a 100% natural snowpack across 146.8 hectares on 35 named trails — no snowmaking figure appears in the plan, so season length is a weather fact, not an operator promise.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Hemlock?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 9 condos and townhomes listed in Hemlock. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Hemlock a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Hemlock had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Hemlock from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 1 condos and townhomes sold in Hemlock over those 4 months, out of 37 in all of Mission.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: Is Hemlock Valley part of Mission?
faq.a: No. SnapStats groups the "Hemlock" sub-area under the community Mission and many listings carry a Mission mailing address, but Hemlock Valley is unincorporated FVRD Electoral Area C land governed by the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan; it is not inside the City of Mission, and Agassiz mailing addresses do not make it District of Kent land either. Title, zoning, permits and taxes run through the FVRD and the Province.

faq.q: Strata or non-strata — what townhouse can I actually buy here?
faq.a: One verified townhouse strata: the Sakwi Creek Road strata at 20959 Sakwi Creek Road (dwelling type Townhouse, Freehold Strata, built 1997, no complex name published).

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to, and what is the penalty?
faq.a: The Province — rural-area properties receive their tax notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office. Rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid on October 31 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11). Mission's flat 10% city penalty and Chilliwack's city dates do not apply here.

faq.q: Can I rent my Hemlock townhouse out?
faq.a: The valley's pattern is vacation and short-term use (the FVRD describes the dwellings as mainly vacation homes and short-term rentals), and long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been void province-wide since Nov 24, 2022. But a specific unit's permission stack — strata bylaws on short-term rental, FVRD rules, and any licensing — is parcel-level and UNCONFIRMED until the Form B and the FVRD position are read. One Snowflake Crescent listing states there is no short-term rental ban for Hemlock Valley; that is listing copy, not a bylaw record.

faq.q: Is the Snowflake Crescent half duplex a townhouse?
faq.a: No — its listing records dwelling type Half Duplex, Freehold Strata, Plan NWS2041, built 1981.
